content.tagline: Inventory every agent skill, find what's wrong, and manage it safely.

gallery.caption: Global and per-project inventory, with each skill's real link state: symlink, dangling or drift.
Findings from deterministic rules and heuristics, each shipped with the evidence that produced it.

features.name: Inventory
features.subtitle: Across 90+ known agents
features.description: Scans global, per-project and custom directories, then reports the source, the lock metadata and the real link state of every skill: symlinked, dangling, or a drifted copy.

features.name: Trigger profiling
features.subtitle: Positive and negative
features.description: Extracts what dispatches each skill from when_to_use, dispatch_intent, descriptions and "When to Use" sections. You can annotate triggers by hand in a sidecar; skill files are never rewritten.

features.name: Analysis
features.subtitle: Deterministic and heuristic
features.description: Deterministic rules read disk facts: dangling links, missing lock records, copy drift, local edits, cross-scope shadowing and source conflicts. Heuristics surface trigger overlap, negative contradictions and body duplication, each with a confidence score.

features.name: AI evaluation
features.subtitle: Optional, your own key
features.description: Score every skill with your own model, then judge the pre-filtered duplicate and conflict candidates. Results are saved with a signature, so the UI can tell you when an evaluation has gone stale.

features.name: Projects
features.subtitle: Auto-discovered
features.description: Finds projects under your scan roots by their agent markers. Pin the ones you revisit. The registry stores paths only, and removing an entry never deletes a file.

features.name: Remote search
features.subtitle: skills.sh leaderboard
features.description: Browse the public index and the all-time, trending and hot leaderboards, read a SKILL.md before you commit, then install straight into the current scope.

features.name: Safe operations
features.subtitle: One install path
features.description: Every change streams progress into a drawer with a confirmation step and can be cancelled. Writes are delegated to the official skills CLI, so there is one install path, not two.

principles.title: Reads are local and offline
principles.description: Scanning uses the filesystem and lock files only. No network call is required to inventory or analyze your skills.

principles.title: Writes are delegated
principles.description: Every install, update and removal runs through the official skills CLI. SkillCat never becomes a second source of truth, and never edits your files behind your back.

principles.title: Analysis is explainable
principles.description: Deterministic rules and heuristics are labelled separately, and every finding ships with the evidence that triggered it.

principles.title: AI is optional and explicit
principles.description: Scoring and duplicate judgement run only when you ask, with your own key and endpoint. Nothing leaves your machine by default.

faq.q: How is this different from running the skills CLI on its own?
faq.a: The CLI installs skills. SkillCat shows you the state of everything you have already installed: it reads what the CLI and your agents wrote to disk, explains each skill, and flags concrete problems before they bite.

faq.q: Does it need an API key?
faq.a: No. Inventory, trigger profiling and the rule engine all run without a model. An API key is only needed if you switch on the optional AI evaluation.

faq.q: Which agents does it know about?
faq.a: Over 90 known agent directories, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Windsurf and Trae. You can add your own skill directories as well.

Not silently. Scanning is read-only, and annotations live in a sidecar file in the config directory. Any change to a skill directory goes through the official skills CLI, with an explicit confirmation step.

faq.q: What do I need to run it?
faq.a: macOS is self-contained: the skills CLI is bundled, so no Node.js install is required. On Windows, install Node.js 22 or newer.

footer.ethos: Local-first. Read-only by default. One install path.
